spec: Simulate the operation of an industrial printing press. The entry function is `printrun(batches)`. The input is a list of tuples containing color, page count, and speed as a string. spec: Simulate an aquarist feeding various marine exhibits. The entry function is `feed(tanks)`. The input is a list of tuples containing tank name, species, and food weight. title: Baking Competition Judging
spec: Write a function `judge(cakes)` that evaluates a list of dessert qualities. Emit a welcoming the bakers speech. For each quality, provide feedback. If the quality is underbaked, emit a soggy bottom warning. If it is perfect, emit a special handshake approval. If it is burnt, emit a bitter taste criticism. For any other quality, emit a generic pleasant flavor remark. After tasting all entries, emit an elimination announcement. Then emit a star baker award declaration. Finally, emit a cleaning the tent instruction. Example: judging ['underbaked', 'perfect', 'dry'] outputs the culinary critiques and the final awards.

title: Deep Space Probe Telemetry
spec: Write a function `transmit(packets)` that processes a list of instrument sources. Emit a solar system departure alert. For each source, detail the analysis. If the source is a camera, emit an image received confirmation. If it is a spectrometer, emit a composition analyzed report. If it is a magnetometer, emit a magnetic field measured alert. For any other source, emit a background radiation reading. Once transmission completes, emit a power level critical warning. Then emit a final goodbye message. Finally, emit a shutdown sequence confirmation. Example: receiving data from ['camera', 'magnetometer', 'radar'] displays the telemetry logs and the probe shutdown steps.

title: Cable Car Journey
spec: Write a function `operate(stations)` that handles a list of mountain elevations. Emit a passenger boarding confirmation. Loop through the elevations. If the elevation is low, emit a crossing river observation. If it is medium, emit a changing gears sound. If it is high, emit a summit reached celebration. For any other elevation, emit a scenic valley view description. Upon reaching the end, emit a disembarking instruction. Then emit a securing brakes notification. Finally, emit a motor shutdown sequence. Example: passing ['low', 'high', 'unknown'] outputs the travel sights and the operational checks.

title: Safecracking Heist
spec: Write a function `crack(tumblers)` that reviews a list of lock mechanisms. Emit a stethoscope application action. For each mechanism, describe the interaction. If it is stiff, emit an applying oil instruction. If it is clicking, emit a pin set confirmation. If it is jamming, emit a reversing direction action. For any other mechanism, emit a gentle tapping action. After bypassing all mechanisms, emit a handle pulling description. Then emit a door swinging open sound. Finally, emit a bagging the loot instruction. Example: feeling ['stiff', 'clicking', 'loose'] logs the burglary attempts and the successful vault opening.

title: Art Gallery Opening
spec: Write a function `exhibit(artworks)` that processes a list of painting styles. Emit a champagne pouring introduction. For each style, gauge the reaction. If the style is abstract, emit a confused murmur description. If it is a portrait, emit a gasp of recognition. If it is a landscape, emit a peaceful sigh observation. For any other style, emit a polite clapping sound. Following the walkthrough, emit a painting sold announcement. Then emit a locking the doors instruction. Finally, emit a turning off lights action. Example: viewing ['abstract', 'portrait', 'modern'] documents the guest reactions and the closing procedures.

title: Vintage Photograph Development
spec: Write a function `develop(film)` that processes a list of chemical stages. Emit a red light activation confirmation. Iterate through the stages. If the stage is developer, emit an image appearing observation. If it is stop bath, emit a halting reaction notice. If it is fixer, emit a making permanent declaration. For any other stage, emit a gentle agitation instruction. After the baths, emit a water washing step. Then emit a hanging to dry action. Finally, emit an inspecting final negative description. Example: passing ['developer', 'fixer', 'rinse'] details the darkroom process and the final image review.

title: Orchestral Tuning Sequence
spec: Write a function `tune(instruments)` that takes a list of musical sections. Emit a conductor entering stage description. For each section, guide the warmup. If the section is strings, emit a bowing a note instruction. If it is woodwinds, emit a warming up reeds action. If it is brass, emit a clearing spit valves action. For any other section, emit a light percussion tap. After all sections prepare, emit a full chord sounding description. Then emit an audience quieting observation. Finally, emit a raising arms to begin instruction. Example: preparing ['strings', 'brass', 'timpani'] outputs the concert hall sounds and the performance start.

title: Icebreaker Ship Navigation
spec: Write a function `steer(ice)` that evaluates a list of frozen obstacles. Emit a diesel engine startup sequence. For each obstacle, detail the maneuver. If the ice is thin, emit a slicing through easily observation. If it is medium, emit a hull shuddering warning. If it is thick, emit a backing up to ram action. For any other obstacle, emit a steering around iceberg instruction. Once clear, emit an open water reached confirmation. Then emit a polar bear spotted observation. Finally, emit an arriving at research station announcement. Example: passing ['thin', 'thick', 'unknown'] will trigger the corresponding obstacle alerts along with the startup and concluding announcements.

title: Lumberjack Tree Felling
spec: Write a function `chop(trees)` that processes a list of wood types. Emit a sharpening axe preparation. Loop through the wood types. If the wood is pine, emit a quick chopping sound. If it is oak, emit a heavy swinging effort. If it is birch, emit a peeling bark observation. For any other wood, emit a standard felling action. After processing the forest section, emit a yelling timber warning. Then emit a tree falling crash description. Finally, emit a resting on a stump action. Example: cutting ['pine', 'oak', 'maple'] outputs the physical labor descriptions and the final timber events.

title: Cave Maze Explorer
spec: Create a script to navigate a subterranean maze. The entry point is a function named `explore(moves)` taking a list of string directions. Before processing, output the starting coordinates zero zero. For each direction in the list, check its value. If north, output moving north and increase the vertical position. If south, output moving south and decrease the vertical position. If east, output heading east and increase the horizontal position. If west, output heading west and decrease the horizontal position. If the direction is jump, output leaping forward and increase both positions by two. If wait, output pausing to rest. For any other direction, output invalid direction followed by the direction string. After processing all directions, output the final coordinates. For example, given a list containing north and jump, it outputs moving north then leaping forward. Include a main section to run this.

title: Vintage Text Editor
spec: Build a simulated line-based text editor. The main function `edit(commands)` receives a list of instruction strings. Start by outputting starting editor. Maintain a list of text lines. For each instruction, apply these rules: If it starts with add, append the rest of the string to the lines and output line added followed by the current line count. If it is delete, remove the last line and output line deleted, or output buffer empty if there are no lines. If it is show, output the entire text joined by spaces. If it is save, output saving file followed by the total character count. If it is clear, empty the list and output buffer cleared. If it is exit, output shutting down and terminate the loop. Otherwise, output unknown instruction followed by the command. For example, given a list containing add hello and show, it outputs line added followed by the line count, then hello. Run the function in a main block with a realistic sequence of instructions.

title: Veterinary Triage
spec: Write a medical evaluation system for an animal clinic. The entry function `diagnose(symptoms)` takes a list of symptom strings. Begin by outputting patient evaluation started. Evaluate each symptom in order. If bleeding, output critical emergency followed by immediate surgery required. If vomiting, output monitor hydration and the symptom name. If limping, output schedule x ray for the limb. If lethargy, output check temperature and run blood test. If coughing, output isolate patient and administer antibiotics. If scratching, output check for fleas or allergies. For any unrecognized symptom, output standard observation followed by the symptom string. Once all items are evaluated, output evaluation complete followed by the total number of symptoms processed. For example, given a list containing bleeding and scratching, it outputs critical emergency followed by immediate surgery required, then check for fleas or allergies. Execute the logic with a sample list of patient symptoms.

title: Mock Compiler
spec: Design a basic simulator for compiling pseudo code. The main function `assemble(lines)` accepts a list of code strings. First, output compiler initialized. Iterate through the lines. If a line contains let, output variable declaration found. If it contains add or sub, output arithmetic operation detected. If it contains print, output output statement parsed. If it contains if, output conditional branch generated. If it contains loop, output loop structure created. If it contains error, output compilation aborted followed by the line index, and stop the process immediately. For any other text, output unknown syntax on line followed by the line index. If the entire list is processed without aborting, output compilation successful. For example, given a list containing let and add, it outputs variable declaration found then arithmetic operation detected. Provide a driver section that tests the simulator.

title: Town Mayor Simulator
spec: Develop a resource management simulator for a small town. The entry function `govern(events)` takes a list of town event strings. Output town simulation started at the very beginning. For each event, determine the appropriate response. If earthquake, output dispatching rescue teams and allocate emergency funds. If festival, output celebrating with citizens and note the current event index. If strike, output negotiating with union leaders. If flood, output building sandbag walls and evacuating low areas. If harvest, output storing surplus food for winter. If crime, output increasing police patrols. For anything else, output logging minor event followed by the event name. End the process by outputting simulation ended followed by the total number of events handled. For example, given a list containing flood and harvest, it outputs building sandbag walls and evacuating low areas, then storing surplus food for winter. Use a main block to run a simulated year of events.

title: Tennis Match Umpire
spec: Create an automatic scoring system for a sports match. The main function `umpire(points)` receives a list of strings indicating the point winner, either player one or player two. Start by outputting match commences. Maintain a numeric score for each side. For each point, if player one wins, increment their score and output point to player one followed by their score. If player two wins, increment their score and output point to player two followed by their score. If both scores reach exactly forty, output deuce reached. If a player exceeds forty and is ahead by two or more, output game awarded to that player and reset both scores to zero. If a player exceeds forty but is ahead by only one, output advantage to that player. If an invalid string is encountered, output fault and the string. At the end of the list, output match suspended. For example, given a list containing player one and player two, it outputs point to player one, then point to player two.

title: Tax Return Auditor
spec: Implement a financial review tool. The core function `audit(records)` processes a list of transaction tuples, each containing a category string and an amount integer. Output audit initiated to start. For each transaction, apply the following logic: If the amount is less than zero, output warning negative balance followed by the amount. If the amount exceeds ten thousand, output large transaction flagged for review. If the amount is exactly zero, output empty record ignored. If the category is donation, output charitable deduction applied. If the category is entertainment, output non deductible expense found. If the category is salary, output income verified. For any other category, output standard review for the category. After the loop, output audit completed followed by the net sum of all amounts. For example, given a list of tuples containing donation and fifty, then salary and two thousand, it outputs charitable deduction applied then income verified. Include a driver to process sample transactions.

title: Mars Rover Operator
spec: Write a navigation script for a planetary exploration vehicle. The function `drive(commands)` accepts a list of terrain strings. Output rover activated when starting. For each terrain type encountered: If crater, output adjusting suspension for crater. If rock, output deploying rock drill and the current step index. If sand, output engaging four wheel drive for sand. If ice, output melting ice for water sample. If alien, output transmitting unknown lifeform data to earth and halt the entire sequence. If dust, output wiping solar panels. For any other terrain, output normal driving over the terrain. When the sequence finishes naturally, output rover entering sleep mode. For example, given a list containing crater and dust, it outputs adjusting suspension for crater then wiping solar panels. Test the logic by running it with a variety of terrain strings.

title: Job Interviewer
spec: Build a simulator for screening employment candidates. The function `interview(responses)` takes a list of candidate answer strings. Output starting interview process initially. Process each response sequentially. If the answer is brief, output asking for more details. If it is comprehensive, output noting excellent communication skills. If it is confused, output repeating the question. If it is silence, output awkward pause detected. If it is aggressive, output candidate rejected due to attitude and terminate the interview immediately. If it is humorous, output laughing and giving bonus points. For any other type of response, output writing down notes for the response. If the list is exhausted without termination, output scheduling follow up round. For example, given a list containing brief and silence, it outputs asking for more details then awkward pause detected. Run a simulation in a main block.

title: Puppy Obedience Trainer
spec: Create a pet training simulator. The main function `train(commands)` processes a list of command strings given to a dog. Output training session begins. Iterate over the commands. If sit, output dog sits and receives a treat. If stay, output dog stays in place. If fetch, output dog chases the ball and the current throw number. If roll, output dog rolls over happily. If jump, output dog jumps up and gets a scolding. If bark, output dog barks loudly at a squirrel. For any unrecognized command, output dog tilts head in confusion at the command. After processing all items, output training session over. For example, given a list containing sit and roll, it outputs dog sits and receives a treat then dog rolls over happily. Provide a main block to exercise the function with a sequence of instructions.

title: Diplomatic Envoy
spec: Design a political negotiation simulator. The core function `negotiate(dialogues)` accepts a list of action strings from a foreign diplomat. Output summit started. Process each action. If the action is demand, output rejecting outrageous demand and increase a tension counter. If it is concede, output accepting concession and decrease tension. If it is threaten, output issuing counter threat and increase tension by two. If it is bribe, output refusing unethical offer and report to council. If it is apologize, output accepting formal apology. If it is propose, output reviewing proposal carefully and the action index. For any other action, output noting diplomatic pleasantry. Once all actions are handled, output summit concluded followed by the final tension level. For example, given a list containing apologize and demand, it outputs accepting formal apology then rejecting outrageous demand.

title: Silk Road Merchant
spec: Write an economic trading journey simulator. The function `trade(actions)` takes a list of market activity strings. Output market stalls open. For each activity: If buy silk, output purchasing fine silk for coins. If sell spices, output trading spices for profit. If haggle, output arguing over prices with a local merchant. If bandit, output losing goods to a bandit ambush and stop the journey completely. If tax, output paying the local lord a tariff. If rest, output staying at a local inn to recover. For any other string, output exchanging common goods. If the journey concludes without being stopped, output arriving safely at the final destination. For example, given a list containing buy silk and tax, it outputs purchasing fine silk for coins then paying the local lord a tariff. Set up a sample journey to demonstrate the logic.

title: Medieval Siege Defender
spec: Implement a castle defense simulator. The entry function `defend(attacks)` receives a list of incoming siege engine strings. Output manning the battlements at the start. For each attack in the sequence: If catapult, output bracing for boulder impact and reduce the wall strength counter. If battering ram, output pouring boiling oil on the gates. If ladders, output pushing ladders off the walls. If siege tower, output firing flaming arrows at the tower. If sappers, output digging counter tunnels. If trebuchet, output taking heavy damage from trebuchet strike. For any other attack, output defending against standard infantry. At the end of the assault, output siege repelled successfully along with the remaining wall strength. For example, given a list containing catapult and sappers, it outputs bracing for boulder impact then digging counter tunnels. Run a test defense in the main scope.

title: Noir Detective
spec: Create a crime scene investigation tool. The function `investigate(clues)` takes a list of discovered evidence strings. Output opening the case file. Loop through the evidence. If fingerprint, output matching prints to the database. If blood, output sending sample to the lab. If weapon, output dusting the weapon for prints. If alibi, output verifying suspect location. If confession, output case solved immediately and stop the investigation loop. If footprint, output measuring shoe size and tread pattern. For any other evidence, output pinning clue to the conspiracy board. If the evidence runs out without finding a confession, output case remains unsolved. For example, given a list containing fingerprint and alibi, it outputs matching prints to the database then verifying suspect location. Test the tool with a mock list of clues.

title: Chaotic Diner Cook
spec: Develop a restaurant kitchen simulator. The function `cook(actions)` processes a list of food order strings. Output tying the apron. Evaluate each order. If soup, output simmering broth for minutes. If steak, output grilling meat to medium rare. If salad, output tossing fresh greens. If fire, output grabbing the fire extinguisher and evacuate the kitchen, terminating the shift. If pie, output baking dessert in the oven. If drop, output cleaning up spilled food from the floor. For any other order, output plating standard meal. Unless the shift was terminated, output untying the apron at the very end. For example, given a list containing soup and steak, it outputs simmering broth for minutes then grilling meat to medium rare. Include a main section that runs a busy shift.

title: Island Castaway
spec: Write a daily survival log for a stranded explorer. The entry function `survive(events)` receives a list of daily occurrence strings. Output washed ashore. Go through each occurrence. If rain, output collecting fresh drinking water. If boar, output hunting for meat and hide. If ship, output lighting the signal fire and cheering. If storm, output hiding in the cave until it passes. If berries, output eating wild fruit and hoping it is safe. If injury, output resting and applying herbal remedies. For anything else, output surviving another quiet day. After surviving the entire list, output writing another notch on the tree followed by the total days survived. For example, given a list containing rain and berries, it outputs collecting fresh drinking water then eating wild fruit and hoping it is safe. Demonstrate the simulation with a sample list.

title: Cyber Mainframe Infiltrator
spec: Build a terminal infiltration simulator. The core function `hack(commands)` accepts a list of system instruction strings. Output neural link established. Process each instruction. If ping, output node response time measured. If decrypt, output breaking encryption keys. If firewall, output bypassing security countermeasures. If trace, output active trace detected disconnecting now and instantly halt the execution. If download, output extracting confidential files. If stealth, output hiding digital footprints in the logs. For any other text, output executing unrecognized shell command. If the system is not halted, output jacking out of cyberspace at the end. For example, given a list containing ping and stealth, it outputs node response time measured then hiding digital footprints in the logs. Use a driver to test the simulator.

title: Galactic Emperor
spec: Create a space empire management system. The function `rule(decisions)` takes a list of imperial decree strings. Output ascending the chromium throne. For each decree in the list: If colonize, output dispatching colony ships to new sectors. If tax, output raising imperial credits and angering citizens. If rebel, output deploying stormtroopers to crush the uprising. If fleet, output constructing new star destroyers. If trade, output signing commerce treaty with aliens. If assassinate, output surviving an attempt on the emperor life. For any other decree, output issuing standard imperial edict. Upon finishing the list, output returning to the royal chambers. For example, given a list containing colonize and fleet, it outputs dispatching colony ships to new sectors then constructing new star destroyers. Test the decrees with a sample run.

title: Post Office Sorter
spec: Implement a package routing system. The main function `sort(parcels)` accepts a list of package type strings. Output conveyor belt started. Examine each parcel. If fragile, output applying bubble wrap and handle with care sticker. If heavy, output assigning to the freight team. If international, output checking customs declaration forms. If express, output routing to the priority overnight bin. If hazard, output moving to quarantine and call security. If letter, output passing through the automated scanner. For any other type, output sorting into the standard domestic bin. At the conclusion of the shift, output turning off the conveyor belt followed by the parcel count. For example, given a list containing fragile and heavy, it outputs applying bubble wrap and handle with care sticker then assigning to the freight team. Execute the sorter in a main block.

title: Emergency Room Triage
spec: Develop a hospital patient sorting system. The function `treat(patients)` takes a list of medical condition strings. Output doors open for patients. Iterate through the conditions. If cardiac, output code blue calling the resuscitation team. If trauma, output preparing the trauma bay and surgical consult. If fever, output administering antipyretics and drawing blood. If fracture, output ordering splint and orthopedic review. If stroke, output activating stroke protocol and sending to imaging. If minor, output directing to the fast track waiting room. For any other condition, output taking vital signs and assigning a bed. Finally, output shift completed. For example, given a list containing fever and minor, it outputs administering antipyretics and drawing blood then directing to the fast track waiting room. Include a short driver simulating a shift.

title: Intersection Controller
spec: Write a traffic management script. The function `direct(vehicles)` processes a list of approaching vehicle strings. Output traffic lights operational. For each vehicle: If ambulance, output turning all lights red for emergency vehicle. If bus, output extending green light for mass transit. If bicycle, output activating the bike lane signal. If pedestrian, output engaging the crosswalk countdown. If speeding, output flashing warning sign for fast vehicle. If heavy truck, output calculating clearance time for large load. For any other vehicle, output standard green light cycle. When the list ends, output intersection going to flashing yellow. For example, given a list containing bus and bicycle, it outputs extending green light for mass transit then activating the bike lane signal. Use a sample sequence of vehicles to run the system.

title: Music Festival Coordinator
spec: Create a live event scheduling simulator. The main function `organize(bands)` receives a list of status update strings. Output gates open to the public. Process each status sequentially. If delayed, output pushing back the set time and informing the crowd. If arrived, output showing the band to their dressing room. If soundcheck, output adjusting the audio monitors for the stage. If playing, output turning on the stage lights and pyrotechnics. If rain, output covering the equipment with tarps. If curfew, output cutting the power to the main stage and stop processing updates. For anything else, output broadcasting background music over the speakers. At the end, output festival grounds closed. For example, given a list containing arrived and soundcheck, it outputs showing the band to their dressing room then adjusting the audio monitors for the stage.

title: Subterranean Spelunker
spec: Implement a cave exploration logging tool. The function `navigate(hazards)` accepts a list of underground obstacle strings. Output turning on the headlamp. Go through each hazard. If chasm, output anchoring the rope and repelling down. If squeeze, output taking off the backpack and crawling through. If bats, output turning off the light and staying quiet. If water, output inflating the raft to cross the underground river. If collapse, output running back to the entrance and terminate the expedition. If crystal, output marveling at the giant gypsum formations. For any other obstacle, output walking carefully over loose rocks. If not terminated, output emerging into the daylight. For example, given a list containing chasm and bats, it outputs anchoring the rope and repelling down then turning off the light and staying quiet. Test the logic with a sample exploration.

title: Antique Roadshow Expert
spec: Develop a valuation simulator for historical items. The core function `appraise(items)` takes a list of antique description strings. Output setting up the appraisal table. Evaluate each item. If painting, output examining the brushstrokes and signature. If coin, output checking the mint mark and wear level. If furniture, output inspecting the dovetail joints and wood type. If jewelry, output testing the gemstones and metal purity. If forgery, output calling security and confiscating the fake, then halt the session. If toy, output checking the original packaging and moving parts. For any other description, output giving a rough estimate based on condition. At the end, output packing up the magnifying glass. For example, given a list containing coin and toy, it outputs checking the mint mark and wear level then checking the original packaging and moving parts.

title: Professional Wrestling Booker
spec: Write a sports entertainment match simulator. The entry function `referee(moves)` receives a list of wrestling maneuver strings. Output ringing the opening bell. For each maneuver: If suplex, output slamming the opponent onto the mat. If submission, output asking the wrestler if they want to quit. If chair, output warning the wrestler about disqualification. If interference, output ejecting the manager from ringside. If finisher, output counting one two three and ring the bell to end the match, stopping further processing. If taunt, output telling the wrestler to focus on the match. For any other maneuver, output watching the action closely. If the match concludes, output raising the winner hand. For example, given a list containing suplex and taunt, it outputs slamming the opponent onto the mat then telling the wrestler to focus on the match.

title: Glassblowing Studio Session
spec: Write a function `blow(actions)` that accepts a list of tuples where each tuple contains an action string and a temperature integer. First, print a message that the studio furnace is hot. Then loop through the list. If the action is gather, print gathering glass at the given temperature. If the temperature is over two thousand, print a warning about intense heat. If the action is roll, print shaping on the marver. If the action is puff, print blowing air into the pipe. If the action is swing, print elongating the shape. If the action is detach, print transferring to the punty. If the action is anneal, print placing in the cooler. If the action is anything else, print pausing to inspect the piece. Finally, print a summary message of the total steps taken. Example input: a list with gather and two thousand one hundred, then puff and one thousand. Example output: the hot furnace message, the gather message, the heat warning, the puff message, and the summary of two steps.

title: Wine Tasting Guide
spec: Write a function `taste(wines)` that takes a list of tuples containing a grape variety string, an age integer in years, and a color string. Before the loop, print setting up the tasting glasses. Iterate through the wines. For each one, print pouring a glass of the variety. If the color is red and age is over five, print noting the brick rim and complex aromas. If it is red and young, print observing the vibrant ruby hue. If the color is white and age is over three, print catching hints of honey and hazelnut. If it is a young white, print enjoying the crisp citrus notes. If the color is rose, print appreciating the delicate pink shade. If the grape is sparkling, print watching the fine bubbles rise. After evaluating all items, print that the tasting session is complete. Finally, print a reminder to drink water between glasses.

title: Hot Air Balloon Flight
spec: Create a function `fly(conditions)` that receives a list of tuples representing wind speed integers and altitude target integers. Start by printing starting the inflation fan, followed by printing igniting the main burner. Loop through the conditions. If the wind speed is over fifteen, print aborting the ascent due to high winds. If the wind speed is low and altitude is below one thousand, print gently rising above the treetops. If the altitude target is over three thousand, print blasting the burner for a high altitude climb. If the altitude target is exactly zero, print preparing for a smooth landing. If the wind speed is moderate, print drifting steadily over the countryside. After the loop, print packing the envelope into the bag. Then print celebrating with a traditional toast.

title: Shoe Cobbler Repair
spec: Develop a script with a main function `repair(shoes)` taking a list of tuples of shoe type, damage type, and material. Initially, print turning on the heavy stitching machine. For each shoe, print inspecting the shoe type. If the damage is a hole and material is leather, print stitching a leather patch over the hole. If the damage is a hole and material is rubber, print applying vulcanized cement to seal the leak. If the damage is a worn sole, print tearing off the old sole and sanding the bottom. If the damage is a broken heel, print hammering a new heel block into place. If the damage is scuffed, print buffing the material with colored polish. If the shoe type is a boot and damage is a zipper, print sewing a heavy duty replacement zipper. At the end, print wiping all items clean, and print boxing the repaired footwear for the customer.

title: Billiard Table Assembly
spec: Implement a function `assemble(parts)` that takes a list of tuples containing component name, material, and weight integer. Begin by printing clearing a large space in the center of the game room, then print laying down the heavy wooden frame. For each part: if the component is slate and weight is over two hundred, print asking friends to help lift the massive stone bed. If the component is slate and material is italian, print marveling at the perfectly flat grey surface. If the component is felt, print stretching the green cloth tightly and stapling it underneath. If the component is rail, print bolting the rubber cushions to the top edges. If the component is pocket and material is leather, print weaving the leather nets into the corner holes. If the component is pocket and material is plastic, print snapping the cheap drop pockets into place. After assembling the list, print rolling a cue ball to check for level, and print racking the colorful balls into a tight triangle.

title: Tarot Card Reading
spec: Write a script with a function `read(cards)` that accepts a list of tuples containing card name, orientation string, and position string. First, print shuffling the deck three times, and print cutting the deck into two piles. Loop through the cards. If the position is past, print looking at the foundation of the situation. If the position is present, print examining the current energies at play. If the position is future, print predicting the likely outcome. If the orientation is reversed, print warning of blocked potential or internal struggle. If the orientation is upright and the card name includes major, print highlighting a significant life event. If the card name includes swords, print focusing on intellect and conflict. After reading all cards, print closing the reading, and print clearing the cards for the next seeker.

title: Vinyl Record Pressing
spec: Design a function `press(batches)` that receives a list of tuples with album name, color variant, and quantity integer. Start by printing turning on the steam valves to heat the press, and print securing the metal stampers into the plates. Loop through the batches. If the color is black, print extruding a standard black vinyl puck. If the color is splatter, print mixing base color pellets with contrasting beads. If the color is clear, print ensuring the hopper is completely clean of dust. If the quantity is over five hundred, print starting a long continuous pressing run. If the quantity is under fifty, print monitoring closely for a short custom run. For every batch, print dropping the puck onto the spindle, and print closing the press with tons of pressure. After the loop, print turning off the steam, and print opening the cooling water valves.

title: Bungee Jump Experience
spec: Create a function `jump(jumpers)` that processes a list of tuples with jumper name, weight integer, and anxiety level string. Begin by printing opening the bridge platform for the day. Loop through the jumpers. If the weight is over two hundred, print attaching the heavy duty thick cord. If the weight is under one hundred, print using the lightest tension cord for a smooth rebound. If the anxiety is high, print talking the jumper through deep breathing exercises. If the anxiety is low, print giving a quick high five and stepping back. For each person, print checking the ankle harnesses twice, print counting down from three, and print shouting bungee and watching them fall. After all jumpers have gone, print lowering the recovery line, and print securing the equipment for the night.

title: Drum Kit Assembly
spec: Write a function `build(components)` that takes a list of tuples representing part name, size string, and material. First print laying down the drum rug on the stage. Loop through the components. If the part is kick drum, print extending the spurs and attaching the pedal. If the part is snare and material is brass, print placing the heavy drum on its stand for a piercing crack. If the part is snare and material is wood, print tuning the batter head for a warm pop. If the part is tom and size is large, print mounting the floor tom on its three legs. If the part is tom and size is small, print clamping the rack tom to the bass drum mount. If the part is hihat, print threading the top cymbal onto the clutch rod. If the part is ride cymbal, print angling the heavy boom stand carefully. After assembling everything, print sitting on the throne, and print playing a quick drum roll to test the setup.

title: Sandcastle Building
spec: Develop a function `sculpt(steps)` accepting a list of tuples with tool used, sand wetness level, and action string. Print finding a flat spot near the high tide line, and print digging a large hole to reach ground water. Loop through the steps. If the tool is bucket and wetness is high, print packing dense mud into the bucket for a solid tower. If the tool is bucket and wetness is low, print struggling because the dry sand crumbles away. If the tool is shovel and action is moat, print carving a deep trench around the perimeter. If the tool is trowel and action is windows, print carefully scraping out small square openings. If the tool is hands and action is wall, print patting the sand together to form a sturdy barrier. If the tool is stick and action is texture, print drawing brick patterns into the facade. After all steps, print placing a small flag on the highest peak, and print taking a picture before the ocean washes it away.

title: Cheese Making Process
spec: Implement a function `culture(milks)` taking a list of tuples with animal source, fat content level, and target cheese type. Start by printing sterilizing the stainless steel vats, and print warming the milk slowly over a water bath. For each item: if the source is goat, print adding specific mesophilic cultures for a tangy flavor. If the source is sheep and fat content is high, print anticipating a rich and creamy yield. If the target is cheddar, print cutting the curd into small cubes and stacking them to expel whey. If the target is brie, print gently ladling the fragile curds into round molds. If the target is blue, print piercing the wheels with needles to let air feed the mold. If the target is mozzarella, print stretching the hot curd until it becomes shiny and elastic. After processing the list, print moving the wheels to the aging cave, and print wiping down the tables with sanitizer.

title: Bicycle Repair Shop
spec: Design a function `tune(bikes)` that accepts a list of tuples containing brake type, gear count integer, and issue string. First print clamping the bicycle frame into the repair stand. For each bike: if the brake type is hydraulic, print bleeding the fluid lines to remove air bubbles. If the brake type is rim, print replacing the rubber pads and centering the calipers. If the gear count is one, print tensioning the single chain to prevent dropping. If the gear count is over ten, print adjusting the derailleur limits to ensure crisp shifting. If the issue is flat tire, print prying off the tire and patching the inner tube. If the issue is broken spoke, print lacing a new steel wire and truing the wheel. If the issue is squeak, print greasing the bottom bracket bearings. After completing the repairs, print wiping the frame with a rag, and print taking the bike for a quick test ride around the block.

title: Clockmaker Restoration
spec: Write a function `restore(clocks)` that takes a list of tuples with era string, mechanism type, and condition. Begin by printing laying out brass tweezers and magnifying loupes on the desk. For each clock: if the era is antique and condition is rusty, print soaking the gears in an ultrasonic cleaning bath. If the era is modern, print checking the battery contacts for corrosion. If the mechanism is pendulum, print polishing the brass weight and checking the suspension spring. If the mechanism is mainspring, print carefully unwinding the coiled steel to prevent explosive uncoiling. If the condition is missing parts, print operating the miniature lathe to carve a replacement pinion. If the condition is running slow, print adjusting the escapement to speed up the tick rate. After addressing each clock, print applying a micro drop of synthetic oil to the pivots, print closing the wooden case securely, and print winding the clock to observe its rhythm.

title: Tattoo Artist Session
spec: Create a function `ink(clients)` taking a list of tuples with design style, body part, and size string. Print wrapping the chair in protective plastic barrier film, and print pouring black and colored ink into tiny caps. For each client: if the style is traditional, print selecting a thick needle grouping for bold outlines. If the style is realism, print choosing a magnum needle for soft gray shading. If the body part is ribs, print reminding the client to breathe steadily through the painful spots. If the body part is arm, print resting the limb comfortably on the armrest cushion. If the size is large, print dividing the stencil application into multiple overlapping sections. If the size is tiny, print working with intense focus to keep the tiny details sharp. After the session is done, print wiping the area with green soap, and print applying a clear healing bandage over the fresh art.

title: Standup Comedy Routine
spec: Develop a function `perform(jokes)` that receives a list of tuples with topic, crowd reaction, and length string. Start by printing grabbing the microphone off the stand and clearing the throat, and print pacing across the small brick wall stage. For each joke: if the topic is airplane food, print delivering the classic observational setup. If the topic is dating, print telling a self deprecating story about a recent date. If the crowd reaction is laughs, print pausing confidently to let the audience chuckle. If the crowd reaction is silence, print sweating slightly and rushing to the next punchline. If the crowd reaction is heckle, print firing back a sharp witty insult to the loudmouth in the front row. If the length is long, print building up the elaborate narrative over several minutes. If the length is short, print dropping a quick clever one liner. After the set, print thanking the city and wishing them a good night, and print waving to the crowd before walking behind the curtain.

title: Tailgating Party Setup
spec: Implement a function `tailgate(activities)` that processes a list of tuples with time until game integer, weather, and action. Print lowering the pickup truck tailgate and opening the coolers. Loop through the activities. If the weather is rainy, print popping up the canopy tent to keep everyone dry. If the weather is sunny, print applying sunscreen and handing out sunglasses. If the time is over three hours and action is food, print firing up the charcoal grill for slow cooking. If the time is under one hour and action is food, print quickly passing out hot dogs and chips. If the action is games, print setting up the wooden boards for a beanbag toss. If the action is music, print connecting the bluetooth speaker and playing team anthems. If the time is zero, print packing the trash bags to leave no trace. After the activities, print locking the vehicle doors, and print walking toward the stadium entrance with the tickets.

title: Locksmith Key Duplication
spec: Design a function `duplicate(keys)` accepting a list of tuples with key profile, metal type, and cut count integer. Print turning on the grinding wheel motor. For each key: if the key profile is automotive, print inserting a transponder blank and programming the chip. If the key profile is residential, print clamping a standard brass blank into the vice. If the metal type is steel, print feeding the blade slowly to avoid sparking and wearing down the cutter. If the metal type is aluminum, print sliding the carriage quickly through the soft metal. If the cut count is high, print meticulously tracing the many deep peaks and valleys. If the cut count is low, print making a few simple passes along the edge. For every key made, print running the new key against the wire brush to remove sharp burrs, and print handing the copy to the customer. Finally, print sweeping the metal shavings off the workbench.

title: Soap Making Process
spec: Write a function `saponify(batches)` that takes a list of tuples with oil type, scent, and additive string. First, print putting on safety goggles and thick rubber gloves, and print mixing the lye crystals into the distilled water outdoors. Loop through the batches. If the oil type is olive, print pouring the golden liquid to create a gentle castile bar. If the oil type is coconut, print melting the solid fat to guarantee a rich lather. If the scent is lavender, print stirring in the essential oil as the mixture reaches trace. If the scent is unscented, print leaving the batter pure for sensitive skin. If the additive is oatmeal, print folding in the oats for a soothing exfoliating texture. If the additive is clay, print whisking the colored powder in a separate cup to avoid lumps. After the loop, print pouring the thick batter into the silicone loaf molds, and print covering the molds with towels to insulate the heat.

title: Papermaking Craft
spec: Create a function `pulp(sheets)` receiving a list of tuples with fiber type, dye color, and inclusion. Print filling the large basin with warm water, and print attaching the blender to the power outlet. Loop through the sheets. If the fiber type is cotton, print blending the rags until they form a smooth cloudy pulp. If the fiber type is recycled, print tearing the old newspapers into tiny scraps before soaking. If the dye color is blue, print squeezing a few drops of indigo pigment into the vat. If the dye color is natural, print enjoying the earthy beige tone of the raw fibers. If the inclusion is petals, print sprinkling dried flowers over the floating pulp mixture. If the inclusion is seeds, print adding plantable wildflower seeds to the slurry. For each sheet, print dipping the wooden mould and deckle beneath the surface, and print pulling the frame up flat to catch the fibers evenly. After finishing, print transferring the wet paper onto absorbent felt squares, and print pressing the stack under heavy weights.

title: Bookbinding Workshop
spec: Develop a function `bind(books)` that processes a list of tuples with cover material, binding style, and page count integer. Print sharpening the bone folder and threading the curved needles. For each book: if the binding style is coptic, print sewing thick exposed stitches across the open spine. If the binding style is perfect, print applying hot glue to the clamped text block edge. If the cover material is leather, print skiving the edges thin so they fold neatly over the boards. If the cover material is cloth, print smoothing the fabric over the glued cardboard with a roller. If the page count is over two hundred, print hammering the spine gently to round the thick book. If the page count is under fifty, print folding the thin signature with a single firm crease. After binding all books, print pressing the volumes in the nipping press overnight, print trimming the outer page edges with a heavy guillotine blade, and print admiring the finished handmade journals.

title: Falconry Training Session
spec: Implement a function `train(birds)` accepting a list of tuples with bird species, hunger level, and exercise type. Print pulling on the thick leather gauntlet glove, and print walking out into the open grassy field. Loop through the birds. If the hunger level is low, print leaving the bird on the perch because it will not fly for food. If the hunger level is high, print preparing a small piece of quail meat as a reward. If the species is peregrine and exercise is lure, print swinging the feathered leather lure in wide circles overhead. If the species is hawk and exercise is tree, print releasing the bird into the high branches and calling it down. If the species is owl, print practicing silent flights across short distances. If the exercise is fist, print blowing the whistle and waiting for the bird to land on the glove. After the flights, print securing the jesses to the swivels, and print placing the dark hood over the head to keep the bird calm.

title: Calligraphy Lesson
spec: Design a function `write(strokes)` that takes a list of tuples with script style, pen type, and pressure string. First print ruling light pencil guidelines onto the parchment, and print dipping the nib into the black iron gall ink. Loop through the strokes. If the script style is gothic, print forming sharp angular letters with precise stops. If the script style is copperplate, print writing continuous flowing loops with elegant flourishes. If the pen type is brush, print sweeping the tip lightly for varying line thicknesses. If the pen type is broad, print holding the edge at a consistent forty five degree angle. If the pressure is heavy, print spreading the tines to release a thick pool of ink. If the pressure is light, print barely touching the paper to create a hairline stroke. After the practice, print wiping the metal nibs clean with a damp cloth, and print leaving the paper flat on the desk to dry completely.

title: Stained Glass Crafting
spec: Write a function `craft(pieces)` taking a list of tuples with glass color, shape, and technique string. Print putting on safety glasses and laying out the pattern on the bench, and print turning on the soldering iron to let it heat up. Loop through the pieces. If the glass color is ruby, print holding the beautiful red sheet up to the window light. If the glass color is clear, print cleaning the transparent glass to remove greasy fingerprints. If the technique is score, print dragging the tungsten wheel firmly across the surface to create a break line. If the technique is grind, print pushing the rough edge against the diamond router bit. If the technique is foil, print wrapping the sticky copper tape evenly around the border. If the shape is curve, print using the grozing pliers to gently nibble away the excess glass. After preparing all pieces, print brushing flux over the copper seams, and print melting thick beads of silver solder to fuse the panel together.

title: Kite Flying Afternoon
spec: Create a function `soar(gusts)` that receives a list of tuples with wind strength string, direction, and action. Print assembling the fiberglass rods into the nylon sail, and print tying the thick string to the plastic bridle. Loop through the gusts. If the wind strength is strong and action is launch, print letting go as the kite immediately shoots into the sky. If the wind strength is weak, print running backward desperately to generate some artificial lift. If the direction is shifting, print watching the kite spin out of control toward the ground. If the direction is steady, print standing still and letting the string slide through the fingers. If the action is dive, print pulling the right line hard to execute a dramatic swoop. If the wind strength is gale, print struggling to hold onto the plastic handle as it digs into the palm. After the session, print reeling the string back in a figure eight pattern, and print folding the fabric neatly into its carrying sleeve.

title: Sushi Chef Omakase
spec: Develop a function `serve(courses)` that processes a list of tuples with fish type, preparation method, and garnish. Print tying a white headband and bowing to the seated guests, and print sharpening the long steel willow blade on a wet stone. Loop through the courses. If the fish type is tuna and preparation is raw, print carving a thick ruby slice of fatty belly. If the fish type is eel, print brushing a sweet soy glaze over the warm grilled meat. If the garnish is wasabi, print smearing a tiny green dab under the fish. If the garnish is yuzu, print grating aromatic yellow citrus zest over the top. If the preparation is seared, print igniting the blowtorch to char the delicate skin. If the fish type is sea urchin, print carefully spooning the creamy orange lobes into a seaweed boat. After serving everything, print pouring a small cup of hot green tea for the guests, and print wiping the wooden counter clean with a damp towel.

title: Virtual Microprocessor Emulator
spec: Write a function `emulate(instructions)` that accepts a list of string commands representing machine code. Iterate through the commands while tracking a single accumulator integer starting at zero. If the command starts with load, output a message about the loading action to the screen. If it starts with add, add the following number to the accumulator and output a message showing the addition operation and the new total. Do the same math and output process for subtract, multiply, and divide, providing a specific descriptive output line for each distinct operation type. For jump, output a message about changing the execution pointer, for store output a message about saving to memory, and for halt output a system stop message. Example: providing a list with load ten, add five, halt should result in the console showing the load action, the addition action with the new total of fifteen, and the halting sequence.

title: Dungeon Crawler Command Parser
spec: Implement `parse(commands)` taking a list of player inputs as strings. Process each input through a conditional block. When the input is north, south, east, or west, output a message stating the player walks in that specific direction. If the input is look, display a description of the dark stone walls. If it is inventory, output that the backpack is empty. For take, output that there is nothing to grab. For drop, output that the player has nothing to leave behind. For help, display a short list of available actions, and for quit, output a farewell message and stop processing. Example: providing north, look, quit will display the walking message, the wall description, and the farewell.

title: Minimal Shell Interpreter
spec: Create `execute(commands)` that accepts a list of shell inputs. Maintain a current path string starting at root. Loop over each input. If the command is list, output the simulated directory contents to the console. If it is path, display the current path string. If it is clear, output a screen clearing message. If it is manual, display a help text paragraph. If it is user, output the active username. If the command is network, display a fake IP address string. If it is time, output a mock timestamp. If the command is exit, display a logout message and break the loop. Example: passing path and exit outputs the root string and then the logout message.

title: Transit Kiosk Interface
spec: Develop `kiosk(actions)` that takes a list of simulated button presses for a train ticket machine. For a start action, display a greeting to the customer. For destination, output a message requesting the station name. For adult, output that a full fare ticket was selected. For child, display a message about the discounted youth fare. For bike, output that a bicycle space surcharge is added. For pay, output the payment instruction screen. For ticket, display a message that the paper stub is dispensing. For cancel, output an abort message and reset the transaction. Example: passing start, adult, pay will display the greeting, the full fare confirmation, and the payment prompt.

title: Lunar Terrain Analyzer
spec: Write `analyze(scans)` receiving a list of sensor reading strings from a moon surface rover. Process each reading individually. If the reading is dust, output a message about loose topsoil. If it is basalt, output a finding of volcanic rock. If it is ice, display a message about frozen water deposits. If it is crater, output a warning about steep drops. If it is titanium, display a message noting valuable minerals. If the reading is radiation, output a high exposure alert. If it is signal, display a message about receiving telemetry from earth. If it is error, output a sensor malfunction warning. Example: passing ice and dust outputs the frozen water message followed by the loose topsoil message.

title: Wizard Spell Checker
spec: Create `cast(incantations)` taking a list of magical words. Maintain a mana integer starting at fifty. For the word lumos, deduct five mana and display a message about creating a light source along with the new mana total. For ignis, deduct ten mana and output a fireball description. For glacius, deduct eight mana and display a freezing effect. For aegis, deduct fifteen mana and output a shield generation message. For levita, deduct seven mana and display a floating object message. For mendo, deduct twelve mana and output a healing aura description. For scry, deduct twenty mana and display a vision of the future. If mana drops below zero during any spell, output an exhaustion warning instead of the spell effect. Example: passing lumos outputs the light message and drops mana to forty five.

title: City Grid Power Monitor
spec: Implement `monitor(events)` that processes a list of grid status strings. If the event is surge, display a message about activating safety capacitors. If it is blackout, output an emergency alert for the affected city sector. If it is nominal, display a standard operating message. If it is peak, output a warning about high residential energy demand. If it is solar, display a message about receiving renewable daytime energy. If it is wind, output a message noting turbine contributions. If it is maintenance, display a scheduled downtime notification. If it is offline, output a disconnection error for the main trunk. Example: passing solar and peak displays the renewable energy message followed by the high demand warning.

title: Tectonic Activity Logger
spec: Write `log(tremors)` that takes a list of earthquake magnitude float values. For each value, output a distinct geological assessment. If the magnitude is below two, display a message about micro tremors. If it is between two and three, output a minor shaking notice. Between three and four, display a message about noticeable rattling indoors. Between four and five, output a warning about falling objects. Between five and six, display an alert for potential structural damage. Between six and seven, output a severe destruction warning. Above seven, display a catastrophic event emergency broadcast. If the value is exactly zero, output a message about complete tectonic silence. Example: passing two point five outputs the minor shaking notice.

title: Arboretum Tour Guide
spec: Create `guide(stops)` which accepts a list of tree species names as input. For oak, display a paragraph about strong hardwood and acorns. For maple, output a message describing autumn foliage and syrup. For pine, display information about evergreen needles and cones. For willow, output a story about drooping branches near water. For birch, display a fact about peeling white bark. For sequoia, output a message marveling at the massive height and age. For cherry, display a description of spring blossoms. For palm, output a message about tropical climates and coconuts. If a species is unrecognized, output a generic plant appreciation message. Example: passing pine outputs the evergreen information.

title: Aerial Drone Choreography
spec: Develop `choreograph(moves)` taking a list of formation commands. If the command is circle, output a message directing drones to form a large ring in the sky. If it is square, display an instruction for four sharp corners. If it is star, output a message to create a five pointed shape. If it is helix, display a twisting upward spiral sequence. If it is wave, output a cascading altitude change message. If it is scatter, display an instruction to disperse safely to avoid collisions. If it is land, output a vertical descent sequence. If it is flash, display a strobe lighting effect message. Example: passing circle outputs the ring formation message.

title: Textile Pattern Interpreter
spec: Write `knit(stitches)` taking a list of short instruction codes. For the code knit, display a message to pull the yarn through the front of the loop. For purl, output a message to pull the yarn through the back. For slip, display an instruction to move the loop without knitting. For increase, output a message to create an extra loop on the needle. For decrease, display an instruction to combine two loops into one. For caston, output a message to add a starting loop to the needle. For bindoff, display an instruction to finish the edge. For yarnover, output a message to wrap the yarn around the needle. Example: passing knit and purl displays the front pull message then the back pull message.

title: Telegraph Signal Decoder
spec: Implement `decode(signals)` receiving a list of dot and dash patterns. For a single dot, output the letter E to the screen. For a single dash, display the letter T. For dot dash, output the letter A. For dash dot, display the letter N. For dot dot, output the letter I. For dash dash, display the letter M. For dot dot dot, output the letter S. For dash dash dash, display the letter O. For any empty string or space, output a message indicating a word break. Example: passing dot and dash dash outputs E and then M.

title: Snack Machine Interface
spec: Create `vend(inputs)` that takes a list of user actions. Keep a running balance starting at zero. If the input is coin, increase the balance by one and display the new amount. If it is bill, increase by five and output the updated balance. If it is cola, check if the balance is at least two; if so, deduct two and output a beverage dispensing message, otherwise display an insufficient funds warning. Do the same for chips costing one, candy costing two, and gum costing one, outputting a specific dispensing message for each snack. If the input is refund, output the returned amount and reset the balance to zero. Example: passing bill and gum outputs the five balance, the gum dispensing message, and leaves a balance of four.

title: DNA Mutation Analyzer
spec: Write `analyze(codons)` which takes a list of three letter string sequences. Iterate through the items. If the item is adenine repeated three times, display a message about a lysine amino acid. If it is cytosine repeated three times, output a message for proline. If it is guanine repeated three times, display a message for glycine. If it is thymine repeated three times, output a message for phenylalanine. If the item contains a mix starting with adenine, display a general purine start message. If it starts with cytosine, output a pyrimidine start message. If it is exactly start, display a sequence initiation message. If it is exactly stop, output a sequence termination message. Example: passing start and three adenines displays the initiation message then the lysine message.

title: Console Widget Drawer
spec: Develop `draw(widgets)` accepting a list of user interface element names. For the name button, display a rectangle made of brackets and dashes to standard out. For checkbox, output a set of square brackets with an ex inside. For radio, display parentheses with a lowercase oh inside. For textfield, output a long line of underscores. For label, display a placeholder text string. For divider, output a solid line of equal signs spanning the screen width. For progress, display a row of hash marks. For scrollbar, output a vertical pipe character. Example: passing radio displays the parentheses graphic.

title: Assembly Debate Moderator
spec: Create `moderate(motions)` taking a list of parliamentary procedure strings. For the motion speak, display a message granting the floor to a member. For yield, output a message transferring time to another member. For object, display a formal objection recorded in the minutes. For recess, output a message declaring a short break. For adjourn, display a session ending declaration. For vote, output a message calling for the yeas and nays. For amend, display a notice that the current bill is being modified. For table, output a message postponing the current discussion indefinitely. Example: passing speak and vote outputs the floor grant message followed by the voting call.

title: Synthesizer Patch Controller
spec: Implement `load(patches)` that accepts a list of sound preset names. For the preset piano, output a message setting the oscillators to a percussive decay. For string, display a setting for a slow attack and long release. For brass, output a configuration for sawtooth waves and a closing filter. For bass, display a sub oscillator activation message. For lead, output a message enabling portamento and monophonic mode. For pad, display a chorus effect and wide stereo panning message. For drum, output a noise generator burst setting. For bell, display a frequency modulation and high pitch setting. Example: passing bass displays the sub oscillator message.

title: Datacenter Climate Monitor
spec: Write `monitor(readings)` receiving a list of sensor category strings. For temperature, output a message stating the cooling system is maintaining twenty degrees. For humidity, display a reading of forty percent moisture. For smoke, output a critical fire suppression system alert. For power, display a message that the primary grid is stable. For backup, output a notice that the diesel generators are on standby. For security, display a message that all biometric locks are engaged. For flood, output a warning checking the raised floor sensors. For network, display a message that fiber links are active. Example: passing smoke outputs the fire alert.

title: Cricket Match Umpire
spec: Create `umpire(deliveries)` taking a list of ball outcome strings. For a dot, display a message that no runs were scored. For a single, output a message for one run and strike rotation. For a boundary, display a message cheering a four run hit. For a six, output a message describing the ball flying over the boundary rope. For a wide, display an extra run penalty and an extra delivery signal. For a noball, output a free hit warning and penalty. For a wicket, display a loud appeal and the batsman walking off. For a bye, output a message that runs were scored without hitting the bat. Example: passing boundary and dot displays the four run cheer and then the zero run message.

title: Ham Radio Logbook
spec: Develop `transmit(signals)` accepting a list of transmission types. For the signal test, display a message sending a standard greeting. For cq, output a general call for any station to respond. For roger, display an acknowledgment of the last transmission. For over, output a message indicating the end of a speaking turn. For out, display a sign off message ending the conversation. For emergency, output a priority distress signal. For weather, display a local meteorological update. For location, output a set of geographical coordinates. Example: passing cq and over displays the general call and the turn end message.

title: Cassette Tape Duplicator
spec: Write `duplicate(steps)` receiving a list of machine operation codes. For the code load, display a message about inserting the master tape. For spool, output a message regarding winding the blank magnetic tape. For record, display a message about transferring the audio signal at high speed. For verify, output a message checking the audio quality. For cut, display an instruction to slice the tape to the correct length. For splice, output a message about joining the tape to the leader. For shell, display a message enclosing the tape in the plastic housing. For label, output a message stamping the album artwork on the cassette. Example: passing load and record displays the insertion message and the transfer message.

title: Geocache Navigator
spec: Implement `navigate(waypoints)` taking a list of string instructions for a GPS treasure hunt. For the instruction north, display a message to walk towards the magnetic pole. For south, output a message to head towards the equator. For east, display an instruction to walk towards the sunrise. For west, output a message to head towards the sunset. For search, display an instruction to look under rocks and logs. For find, output a celebratory message about locating the hidden container. For sign, display a message about writing a name in the logbook. For trade, output a message regarding swapping small trinkets. Example: passing north and search displays the magnetic pole message and the looking instruction.

title: Highway Toll Booth Operator
spec: Create `process(vehicles)` taking a list of vehicle type strings. Maintain a daily revenue integer starting at zero. If the vehicle is car, add two to the revenue and output a standard toll message along with the new revenue. If it is motorcycle, add one and display a discounted toll message. If it is truck, add five and output a heavy duty vehicle surcharge message. If it is bus, add four and display a passenger transport message. If it is emergency, add zero and output a message raising the barrier immediately. If it is military, add zero and display an official convoy clearance message. If it is exempt, add zero and output a government vehicle pass message. If it is violation, output a message flashing the camera to capture the license plate. Example: passing car outputs the standard toll and updates revenue to two.

title: Yoga Sequence Instructor
spec: Write `instruct(poses)` which accepts a list of pose names. For the pose mountain, display a message to stand tall and breathe deeply. For downward, output a message to press hips up and back. For plank, display an instruction to hold the body in a straight line. For chaturanga, output a message to lower down slowly. For cobra, display an instruction to lift the chest and look forward. For child, output a resting message to sit back on the heels. For tree, display a balance instruction lifting one foot. For corpse, output a final relaxation message lying flat on the back. Example: passing plank and tree displays the straight line instruction and the balance instruction.

title: Rare Book Archivist
spec: Develop `archive(actions)` taking a list of preservation steps. For the action dust, display a message about using a soft brush on the cover. For inspect, output a message checking the binding for damage. For scan, display a message about digitizing the fragile pages. For catalog, output an instruction to enter metadata into the database. For repair, display a message applying archival glue to the spine. For encapsulate, output an instruction to place the map inserts into mylar sleeves. For box, display a message creating a custom acid free enclosure. For store, output a message placing the item in the climate controlled vault. Example: passing dust and scan displays the brushing message and the digitizing message.

title: Pit Stop Execution
spec: Write a function `pitstop(actions)` that simulates a motorsport pit stop. The input is a list of strings representing tasks to perform. Announce the pit lane entry and the crew preparing their equipment. Iterate through the tasks. If the task involves tires, display the pneumatic gun sounds and the wheel change. If it involves fuel, display the refueling nozzle connection and report a fire safety warning based on the fuel amount. If it involves aerodynamics, report the wing adjustment. After completing all tasks, announce the jack dropping, the driver release signal, and a message concluding the pit stop. Example input: a list containing tire change and refuel.

title: Rally Co Driver Pace Notes
spec: Create a function `navigate(curves)` that acts as a rally navigator. The input is a list of three item tuples containing the distance to the next turn, the direction, and the severity level from one to six. Output the starting line countdown and the transmission engagement. For each turn, output the distance and the turn description. If the severity is five or six, output an urgent caution message to the driver. If the distance is less than fifty meters, output the word into between the current and next turn. If a water splash is mentioned in the description, output a reminder to turn on the wipers. Output the flying finish announcement, the stop control arrival, and the stage time when all turns are completed. Example input: a list with fifty, left, four.

title: Ice Hockey Penalty Shootout
spec: Develop a function `shootout(attempts)` that narrates a game deciding penalty shootout. The input is a list of three item tuples specifying the team name, the player jersey number, and the shot result such as goal, save, or miss. Announce the start of the shootout and the roaring crowd. For each attempt, display the current round number and introduce the shooter stepping up to center ice. Display a specific reaction based on whether the result is a clean goal, a miraculous save by the goaltender, or a heartbreaking miss off the post. Keep a running tally and display the updated score after each shot. Conclude by announcing the winning team and the players rushing the ice. Example input: a list with home team, nineteen, goal.

title: Origami Folding Instructions
spec: Write a function `origami(steps)` that guides a user through creating a paper model. The input is a list of two item tuples containing the fold type and the paper section. Announce the starting square paper size and color preparation. For each step, if the fold is a valley fold, display instructions to fold toward the user. If it is a mountain fold, instruct to fold away. For a squash fold or petal fold, display a complex maneuvering tip. If a reverse fold is encountered, issue a reminder to crease the paper sharply beforehand. Upon finishing all steps, report the final model inspection. Finally, announce the completion of the beautiful paper craft. Example input: a list with valley fold, top right corner.

title: Lathe Machining Steps
spec: Implement a function `machine(operations)` that logs the sequence of actions for a metal lathe. The input is a list of three item tuples indicating the operation type, the cut depth in millimeters, and the spindle speed. Announce the main power on and chuck clamping. For each operation, display the tool selection and the corresponding spindle speed. If the cut depth exceeds three millimeters, issue a heavy load warning to watch for tool chatter. Display the completion of each roughing or finishing pass. Conclude the sequence by announcing the spindle stop, the coolant shutoff, the final dimension check, and the part ejection. Example input: a list with turning, two, five hundred.

title: Demolition Derby Event
spec: Create a function `derby(hits)` that commentates a chaotic car destruction event. The input is a list of three item tuples with the attacker car number, the victim car number, and the damage severity level from one to ten. Announce the green flag dropping and engines roaring. For each hit, report the impact. If the severity is low, display a fender bender remark. If medium, announce a solid crunch. If high, declare a catastrophic smash and announce the elimination of the victim car. Once all hits are processed, announce the checkered flag, the settling smoke, and declare the last car standing as the champion. Example input: a list with seven, forty two, eight.

title: Tandem Skydive Sequence
spec: Write a function `skydive(altitudes)` that logs the events of a tandem parachute jump. The input is a list of descending integer altitudes in feet. Announce the boarding of the aircraft, the safety briefing, and the takeoff roll. As you iterate through the altitudes, display specific actions. At ten thousand feet, announce the door opening and the green light. At nine thousand feet, display the thrilling freefall acceleration. At five thousand feet, announce the main canopy deployment. Lower altitudes should trigger steering check logs and landing pattern setups. Finally, announce the gentle touchdown and harness release. Example input: a list containing ten thousand, five thousand, and zero.

title: Mud Run Obstacles
spec: Develop a function `mudrun(course)` that tracks a participant through an extreme obstacle race. The input is a list of two item tuples containing the obstacle name and its difficulty rating out of five. Announce the starting horn, the participant cheering, and the initial muddy plunge. For each obstacle, report the approach. If the difficulty is four or five, display a message about the intense physical struggle and teamwork required. If lower, display a smooth crossing. If the obstacle is the ice bath, issue a brain freeze warning. Conclude by announcing the finish line crossing, the exhaustion, and the medal presentation. Example input: a list with rope climb, four.

title: Figure Skating Program
spec: Create a function `skate(elements)` that narrates a competitive figure skating routine. The input is a list of two item tuples indicating the element type and the execution quality score. Announce the skater taking their starting pose and the music commencing. For jump elements, display the rotation count and comment on the landing based on the quality score. If a jump combination is detected, display a note on the rapid transition. For spin elements, report the centering and position variations. For step sequences, display a note on the intricate edge work and ice coverage. After processing all elements, announce the final dramatic pose, the audience applause, and the kiss and cry score anticipation. Example input: a list with triple axel, positive two.

title: Whitewater Slalom Run
spec: Implement a function `slalom(gates)` that logs a kayaker navigating a rapid river course. The input is a list of three item tuples containing the gate number, the pole color, and any penalty seconds incurred. Announce the whistle blow, the start beam crossing, and the aggressive initial strokes. For green gates, display a downstream navigation log. For red gates, display a challenging upstream maneuver log. If penalty seconds are greater than zero, report a pole touch and add it to the running penalty total. Report the smooth paddling sections between gates. Finally, announce the finish line crossing, the paddle toss celebration, and display the total accumulated penalty time. Example input: a list with gate one, green, zero.

title: Iditarod Checkpoint Log
spec: Write a function `mush(checkpoints)` that tracks a dog sled team across the frozen tundra. The input is a list of three item tuples detailing the checkpoint name, the resting hours, and the number of dogs dropped from the team for veterinary rest. Announce the ceremonial start in Anchorage and the enthusiastic howling of the pack. For each checkpoint, report the team arrival and the frozen breath in the air.
